mutations.because: The emitter validates before it appends, because a rejected event must never reach the log — not even as garbage a reader would have to reject later. With the launcher gone the operator types --detail by hand, so a malformed payload is likelier, not less likely; accepting it writes a line readEvents must discard and the wave record silently loses the event.

wave-event.sh stamps its own ts and the byte-for-byte comparison feeds that stamp back through formatEvent, so a formatter that re-stamps unconditionally would make the two writers agree only by coincidence of timing — and would silently rewrite the one field a backfilled event depends on. With the launcher gone every event is emitted by hand, so keeping a supplied ts verbatim is what lets a genuinely late event say when it happened.
